s1.syndrome_frame: Acute limb ischemia with cutaneous necrosis in a patient with vascular disease and recent heparin administration
salient_findings: Violaceous pretibial lesions with areas of necrosis
Intense pain in the right lower limb
Necrotic lesion in the right calf
key_facts: 83-year-old man with hypertension and type 2 diabetes mellitus
Admitted for a left foot ulcer secondary to vascular disease
Diagnosed with atrial fibrillation and asymptomatic SARS-CoV-2 infection
No lesion in the site of injection
No history of cocaine use, fever, dyspnea, chest pain, or other systemic symptoms
Antiplatelet antibody test: positive for IgG and polivalent antibodies

raw.syndrome_frame: Acute limb ischemia with cutaneous necrosis in a patient with vascular disease and recent heparin administration
salient_findings: Violaceous pretibial lesions with areas of necrosis
Intense pain in the right lower limb
Necrotic lesion in the right calf
key_facts: 83-year-old man with hypertension and type 2 diabetes mellitus
Admitted for a left foot ulcer secondary to vascular disease
Diagnosed with atrial fibrillation and asymptomatic SARS-CoV-2 infection
No lesion in the site of injection
No history of cocaine use, fever, dyspnea, chest pain, or other systemic symptoms
Antiplatelet antibody test: positive for IgG and polivalent antibodies

differentials: Vasculitis associated with systemic lupus erythematosus
per_call: Vasculitis associated with systemic lupus erythematosus

shortlist.label: Heparin-induced thrombocytopenia
shortlist.why_kept: Recent heparin administration and positive antiplatelet antibody test

shortlist.label: Warfarin-induced skin necrosis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has atrial fibrillation and may be on warfarin, which can cause skin necrosis

shortlist.label: Calciphylaxis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has vascular disease and kidney dysfunction, which are risk factors for calciphylaxis

shortlist.label: Purpura fulminans
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has purpura and necrotic lesions, which are characteristic of purpura fulminans

shortlist.label: Antiphospholipid syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has a history of vascular disease and thrombosis, which are consistent with antiphospholipid syndrome

raw.rationale: The patient was administered subcutaneous abdominal heparin and presented with new skin lesions consisting of violaceous pretibial lesions with areas of necrosis, which is consistent with heparin-induced thrombocytopenia. Additionally, the antiplatelet antibody test was positive for IgG and polivalent antibodies, supporting this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Warfarin-induced skin necrosis
rejected.why: The patient was administered heparin, not warfarin.

rejected.label: Calciphylaxis
rejected.why: There is no mention of calcium or phosphate abnormalities, and the patient's kidney function, while impaired, does not strongly suggest calciphylaxis.

rejected.label: Purpura fulminans
rejected.why: The patient's presentation is not consistent with the typical severe and rapid progression of purpura fulminans, and there is no mention of fever or other systemic symptoms.

rejected.label: Antiphospholipid syndrome
rejected.why: The patient's autoimmunity studies were negative, and there is no other evidence to support this diagnosis.
